text: Oof, I'm finally here! At least the 6 hours went by fast on Delta One! ;)
TATA! You're BACK!
We waited for you for a hundred years.
A hundred MILLION years!
Tata, up! Up up up!
I'm the tallest! Giddyup, Tata!
Hello, Rose. Please keep your arms and legs inside the uncle at all times.
Tata, LOOK. A sparkling diamond gold dumpling squishy!
It's limited edition. There are only two in the whole world. You can squeeze it!
That's the shiniest dumpling I've ever seen. And I've seen a LOT of dumplings.
Come on, Tata! Let's go!
Tata! Deedee made rhubarb crisp for you. It's cooling RIGHT NOW.
I already licked the spoon. Don't tell.
Then we had better hurry. Before somebody licks the rest.
My favorite son!
And my girls! Come here, come here.
Tata, look at the door. Deedee measured me two times since you left.
I got one too. Mine's the low one.
Tom, you must be starving! Sit. The crisp needs ten minutes on the counter.
Where are my reading glasses? I had them one second ago. I need to read the timer.
Deedee. They're on your head.
So they are. Not one word to Boppy.
I brought you a sourdough loaf. Baked it yesterday. It flew here on my lap.
Your bread and my rhubarb crisp. Now THAT is a meal.
A sliver for me. Just a sliver. Sourdough gives me gas.
Mom, EVERYTHING gives you gas.
And I eat it anyway. That's love, Tom.
Tom! Good. I'm not feeling good. It's the stomach.
Deedee! A mud blob just climbed in the window, and it's running off with your crisp!
A WHAT climbed in my window?
It has EYES! The mud has EYES!
Forty years in this kitchen. I've had ants. I've had a raccoon. I have never had THAT.
It's so brown. It's the brownest thing I've ever seen.
That was UNCALLED for!
It's running for the pond!
It took the crisp AND my good tin! Grab your shoes, everybody. We're going after it, and I'm coming with you.
It's headed for Grump Hollow. I've been saying for twenty years that something lives in that pond, and nobody listens to Boppy.
Twenty years ago I'd have caught that thing before it got to the fence.
I'd come with you, but my stomach is acting up. If you see the Big One in that pond, bring him back for me.
Tom. You stay in front of those girls.
Up, up. Everybody up. Deedee kisses it better.
There. Good as new. Try not to do that again.
Look, rhubarb crumbs on the path. The little thief dropped them as it ran, so we can follow the trail.
Tata. The mud is MOVING.
It talks.
It talks AND it steals.
Okay, everybody. Tata is in front. I'm in charge of choreography. FIGHT!
Good job, girls. The crumb trail keeps going north, so that's the way we go.
Ew. Ew ew ew. Nobody touch my hair.
I've been bitten ten thousand times in my life. Not one of them ever said a word first.
Everybody okay? Itchy isn't hurt. Keep walking.
I'm not laughing. I'm giggling. It's different.
Hugs for everyone. There. All better.
The crumbs lead around the pond, toward Boppy's fishing spot.
Boppy says the Big One lives over there.
Then nobody goes near the water. Stay close.
A MARBLE! There's a marble with a bug in it!
That's a dragonfly. It's inside an orange rock. Its wings are open and it's not moving.
Look at the grass. It's grey. Just this bit, the size of my hand.
It isn't dried out. It's just grey. Like somebody took the green out.
I'm keeping it. It's stuck.
Let me.
You're not trying.
I'm trying, Rose. It's a marble and it's winning.
There's a little round hole in the side. Like somebody took a bite.
And somebody left a burnt light bulb. Now they're littering at my pond too.
The tin. Go, go, go.
Bye, marble. I'm coming back for you.
THERE! The thief! He still has the tin!
That's a fish. That fish is bigger than the cab.
Boppy was RIGHT?
Nobody tell him.
That's my GOOD tin, you overgrown handbag!
Tata, he looks like a turtle wearing a hat.
Nobody touches Deedee’s crisp. Everybody ready?
Tom, you stand in front of whoever it stares at. Cozy Rosie, make it laugh. Then we try again.
It has a bug on it! I'm keeping it.
This one you can keep.
Boppy? He comes every day.
Up, up. Everybody up. Deedee kisses it better.
My tin! And look. Half the crisp is still in it.
The Big One ate the other half. I saw crumbs on its chin.
Then we split this half. Everybody home. Wait until Boppy hears about this.
You found the Big One? I TOLD everybody. Twenty years.
Boppy, the mud TALKED. And the mosquitoes. And a puddle.
The mud talked? Forty years in this town, the mud never said one word to me.
We did. And when it laughed, this fell out of its lip.
My LURE! I lost that in 2006. Still shiny. Unlike me.
Keep it, Tom. For luck. The fish clearly didn't want it.
He gave me a present. Look.
That's real gold, Cozy Rosie. Gold like my teeth. Look.
Boppy has treasure in his mouth!
You put that somewhere safe. Gold is for keeping.
Next time something comes in that window, I'm coming. Stomach or no stomach.
Sit. Everybody sit. Half a crisp is still a crisp.
This is the best half a crisp I ever had.
Tata, you're staying the WHOLE week, right?
The whole week. And nobody is stealing anything else.
Slow down. Everybody eats too fast. My stomach.
TNB said he'd be home. Spring Street loft.
Well, well, well...
Look who flew three thousand miles to see me.
My call time got pushed to Thursday. The lead actor lost a shoe. I already found it. So I'm all yours.
Olivia dropped her off this morning. Family trip to the desert. No dogs at the hotel.
She's been sitting on your porch since eight. I tried to take her to the loft. She refused.
Sit, paw, treat. She knows the whole routine. So polite!
Hello, Bready Mercury. Did you miss me? You missed me.
Fifty grams of flour, fifty grams of water. Stir. Look at those bubbles.
I'll take it.
Babe. Look outside. Is the street... purple?
Mr. Washington! Is everything okay?
Excuse me, smog. That was UNCALLED for.
Babe. Remember movie night? You threw the whole popcorn bowl.
Okay. Okay. Everybody breathe. Through the nose. Not the smog.
The smog monsters are gone, but Mr. Washington is still in a daze. Look at him.
Nara is right. That's not kitchen smoke. It's the same purple smog, and it's blowing down from the hills.
Babe. Look north. It's all coming down off the hills.
It's coming from the Observatory. The pipes on its side are pumping out smog like a smoke machine on a bad set.
Then that's where we're going. Nara, stay close.
Up, everybody. Wardrobe says nobody is cut from this scene.
I take the Metro. You have nothing on me.
I contest that ticket, and I'm granting my own appeal. Let's keep going.
Quick wardrobe adjustment, quick heal, and a quick kiss for the road. Ready, babe?
Ready. Kiss accepted. The Observatory is up at the top left. Follow the purple.
The ground is humming. That's never a good sign. I've seen this movie forty-seven times.
Everybody says goodbye. Then they come back. That's what planes are for.
Things have to move.
Well, well, well... looks like we're in a bit of a shaky situation.
Cut. Reset. Back to one, everybody.
Babe, heal right after the Aftershock. When it clogs up, hit it with water or sparkle. Or one of our Tombos.
Look. The sky is blue again. Los Angeles blue. Slightly brown, but blue.
Keep the old windows, though.
Long Island is home, and so is this. I have two homes. Okay. Good.
Um, actually, it's two thousand four hundred and seventy-five. Delta counts every one, and so do I.
How many SkyMiles is that now?
Four hundred and twelve thousand.
Babe! What are you saving them for?
Something really special.
You said that at three hundred thousand.
It has to be REALLY special. But I'd have flown here for zero miles.
Zero miles. Babe. That's the most romantic thing a Delta person can say.
Wait, why is the sky PURPLE? It's two in the afternoon!
It's been like that since this morning. I held my soda up to it. It's the exact same color.
I don't know what it is, babe. But it's pretty grape.
Don't make me laugh, it's freaky! ...Okay. It IS a little grape.
Something strange happened on Long Island too. A blob of mud with eyes climbed in my mother's kitchen window and ran off with her rhubarb crisp.
The mud took Deedee's crisp? Is the mud okay?
We chased it to the pond. And there was a talking fish as big as a car, wearing her baking tin like a crown.
A talking fish! What did he say?
He said "Glub." Then he gave Rose a gold coin.
Mud in the kitchen, a talking fish, and now a purple sky. Babe, something fishy is going on.
The fish was the nicest part!
I want to go look at that sky with you. But first I have to feed Bready Mercury. He's been alone for a week.
He hasn't been alone. Come on, I'll show you.
So I stayed here with her. I was coming over anyway. I've been feeding Bready Mercury every day.
Every day? Fifty grams of flour and fifty grams of water?
Fifty and fifty. I used your little scale.
He got so big he was climbing out of the jar. So I baked a loaf with him.
It's perfectly round! How did you get it so round?
I shaped it on my pottery wheel.
On the pottery wheel! That's brilliant. Why have I been doing it with my hands?
I make bowls all day, babe. So I made you a bread bowl.
A bread bowl! Now we need soup.
Nara, sit.
Paw.
He's twice as big as when I left! What have you been doing with him?
I sing to him while I stir. He's Bready Mercury. He needs his music.
Which songs?
Another One Bites the Crust.
Don't Stop Me Dough!
Babe. That's so good. I'm singing that one tomorrow.
That's the same purple as the sky! An hour ago it was way up on the hill. Now it's on my lawn!
Mr. Washington is sitting out on his porch in that. Come on!
What happened in 1979?
He just said the same thing again, word for word.
He always finishes that story. I've heard it nine times. It ends with gumbo.
It's not a nice afternoon, Mr. Washington! The air is purple!
Babe. That cloud has a face. And it just talked to us.
It's like the mud at my mother's house! I told you they talk!
You did tell me. It's a lot scarier in person.
The man in the mask jumped out! I jumped higher!
And it rained popcorn on the whole room. Let's do that to these clouds.
I don't have any popcorn!
You don't need popcorn. You just need to be that scared.
Oh, I'm that scared.
That doesn't sound like him at all. He tells me how old he is every single morning. He's proud of it!
If the smog did this to him, what about everybody on the boulevard?
Miss Odette and Doña Carmen! Come on!
Miss Odette, it's me! Can I get a bowl of gumbo?
Babe, this is bad. Every time I walk in here she yells "Sit down, you're too skinny!" before the door even closes.
Miss Odette? I'm sorry to bother you. TNB is standing up, and he's very skinny today.
Nothing. She's just like Mr. Washington.
Babe, the pupusas are burning!
Doña Carmen, I'm so sorry. I'm coming behind your counter. I know nobody's allowed back here.
I flipped them. I'm ready for the towel. Go ahead.
She smacks you with that towel if you even look at the griddle.
I know! I've never wanted to be hit with a towel so badly!
The parking tickets can TALK now? They were bad enough when they were quiet!
And I moved my car on Monday night! I set two alarms!
Fine. Can I pay it in SkyMiles?
Excuse me! She is not a snack. She is our guest!
We do have snacks, though. I've got half a bag of gummy worms.
Babe, look at that tree. It's grey. The leaves, the trunk, even the dirt. It looks like an old black and white movie.
There's one lemon on it. And the lemon is inside a block of something orange.
I've seen this before. There's one exactly like it at my parents' pond, with a dragonfly inside.
On Long Island? Babe, that's three thousand miles away.
Two thousand four hundred and seventy-five.
It's not glass, and it's not glaze. I work with this kind of stuff all day and I have no idea what it is.
There's a little round hole in the side, like somebody took a bite out of it.
The one at the pond has the same hole. And you can't pull it off. Rose tried, and then I tried.
Can I try anyway?
Okay. Wow. Your turn.
I already lost to the small one. ...Maybe it's easier in California.
It's not easier in California.
It's a burnt-out flashbulb. My mother found one exactly like it next to the dragonfly.
Who leaves the same bulb at a pond in New York and on a hill in Los Angeles?
I don't know. And I really don't like it.
Me neither. And I like almost everything.
That hill has EYES! The whole hill just stood up!
Babe. I take naps on that hill.
I think you've been napping on his face!
I'm so sorry, sir!
He'd know. He has four hundred and twelve thousand miles.
I'm sorry I kept falling asleep on you. I didn't know you were a person.
It's a gold coin with a lemon on it. Rose's has a dragonfly.
The one the fish gave her?
Yes. A fish gave her one, and now a hill sneezed one at me.
Nara thinks it's a very small frisbee.
Nara, I'm sorry. We don't play fetch with gold.
The hill said a flash woke it up this morning. The fish at the pond said the same thing.
Two flashes, two orange blocks and two gold coins. Babe, I don't love that. Let's go check on Mr. Washington.
That's ten times now. It gets better every time.
Yes, ma'am!
Thank you, Doña Carmen! That's the best towel I've ever been hit with!
Babe. Gumbo. Go get the bread bowl!
It has a hole in the top. I gave that piece to Nara.
That's not a hole. That's where the gumbo goes in.
With two thousand four hundred and seventy-five miles in between.
Each way. That's a lot of SkyMiles.
Tata! Boppy has been waiting by his window since BREAKFAST. He has his fishing hat on.
He said if you were late he'd catch the fish without you. He catches one every time. It's always THIS big.
Then we'd better hurry, before it gets any bigger.
My favorite son!
Tom. Good. Sit down. No. Don't sit down. We're going fishing.
I'm bringing a notebook. For science. And for proof.
And I'm bringing THIS. My pepper jar. Homegrown, pickled in 1989. Older than your mother.
Not one pepper for me either. Peppers give me gas.
Deedee. EVERYTHING gives you gas.
Who told you that.
Tata. At the crisp.
Tata is on thin ice.
I have three pies in, so I'm staying put. Do NOT let him eat peppers on an empty stomach.
I never eat peppers on an empty stomach. I eat them on a full stomach. Then it's empty.
The stomach thanks you. The stomach is still complaining. But it thanks you.
Did I ever tell you about 1970? Sit down. This takes a while.
You did. Forty times.
Then forty-one. First year of college. Cross country. Five miles through the woods, up the big hill, and I never breathed hard.
Last hill, I passed the whole field. Champion. They put my name on a plaque. The plaque is in a box. Somewhere.
Can you still run that fast?
...Sure. Sure I can. I just choose not to. It's bad for the stomach.
Race you to the pier, Boppy!
Last one there's a soggy sock!
Why is everybody walking like they're going to a fire? Slow down! My stomach is doing flips!
Boppy speed, everybody. We walk at Boppy speed.
This is the spot. Forty years, this spot. Now everybody be QUIET.
I AM BEING QUIET.
Rose. Inside voice. Outside.
Shhh. Quiet on the pier, everybody. Boppy has a whole system.
Tom holds the tackle box. I cast. The fish comes. Nobody talks. That's the system.
...Any minute now.
It's been a minute. I wrote it down.
Snack. A pickled pepper settles the stomach.
Deedee said NO peppers.
Deedee isn't here.
TATA! A FISH! A HUGE ONE! WITH A MUSTACHE!
MY JAR!
That was UNCALLED for!
Pickled in 1989. Nobody takes Boppy’s peppers. NOBODY.
Iron-Gill swam west with my jar, into the Whispering Marsh. Come on, we're going after him. And nobody walk fast.
Up. Everybody up. Headcount. One, two, three, four. Good. Nobody is missing. Again.
Tata, that sock has a FACE.
Socks. Out here. Nobody keeps track of their socks anymore.
Excuse me? Nobody gets past ME. That's MY line. I was saying that at Rikers before you were a knot.
Boppy, you're breathing kind of hard.
I'm breathing EXACTLY as hard as I want to.
We take it slow. Iron-Gill’s wake goes northwest, toward those big reeds.
Then we ask it nicely to move. Iron-Gill isn't keeping that jar.
You're sitting on the way to Sundial Hollow. Shove over.
Tata, it's a LOG with a BOOT.
A secret boardwalk. Of course there's a secret boardwalk.
Not secret. Just old. Like me. Nobody comes back here anymore.
The Deep Pool. Nobody has ever seen the bottom. My father said it goes all the way to Ohio.
You took my jar.
Boppy, he's sad! And spicy!
Tom. Tackle box. We do this the old way.
Quiet on the pier, everybody.
Headcount. One, two, three, four. Good.
He belches every third turn, Tom. Heal right after. When he dives, hit the water hard, or do our Tombo.
My jar. Still sealed. Still hot.
And look at that. Forty years, and I finally caught Old Iron-Gill.
Technically he caught your jar, and then we caught him. I'm writing it down anyway. For proof.
Go on, you old bucket. Catch and release. I'll come by. No hooks.
Boppy, can we go home now? I want to tell Deedee EVERYTHING.
Everything except the pepper part.
ESPECIALLY the pepper part.
There they are! Well? Did anybody catch anything?
Nobody believed you.
Deedee! Boppy almost ate a PEPPER! On the pier! Before LUNCH!
Did he.
Hand me my glasses. I want to look at him properly. Where ARE my glasses.
Apron pocket, Deedee!
...Almost isn't eating. Almost is fine.
Sit down, you. I made rhubarb crisp. Everybody sit. And eat SLOWLY.
Slowly. Finally. Somebody in this family gets it.
Best fishing trip ever. Nobody fell in. Mostly.
I love you all to the moon and back. Now eat.
Did they feed you on that plane?
It was Delta One, Mom. They fed me twice.
Twice! You must be starving!
Wait, I have to show you something first. A hill in Los Angeles stood up, talked to us, and sneezed this at me.
A hill stood up? Out there too? First my kitchen, now California!
That's gold like my teeth! Cozy Rosie has one, and now you have one. Where's mine?
You have to get it from a monster, Boppy.
Then I know just the fish. The Whisker Perch. Whiskers like a cat. I saw him at Cattail Pier in 1994, and he was THIS big.
Last time he was only THIS big.
He grew. It's been thirty years.
We believe you now, Boppy. You were right about the Big One.
Say that again, slower. Deary, are you hearing this?
I heard it. Don't let it go to your head. Your hat won't fit.
I believe every fish story you ever told me. I'm bringing the big net.
Mom, there's one more thing. There was a lemon frozen inside an orange block, just like the dragonfly. And this was lying under it.
Same bulb. One at my pond and one three thousand miles away.
Two thousand four hundred and seventy-five.
Tom. Not now.
I don't know what this is and I don't like it. They're both going in the drawer, and all four of you are coming home in one piece. That's not a request.
You said next time you were coming.
Stomach or no stomach. Let's go fishing!
A flash! The fish at the pond said that. So did the hill!
Lightning over my marsh? If anybody's frying that perch, it's me.
I've got the tackle box in one hand and the big net in the other. I'm ready.
Those are WHISKERS! That's him! That's the Whisker Perch! Old Iron-Gill himself!
Boppy, he's way bigger than THIS big. He's bigger than the pier!
I TOLD everybody he grew!
He TALKS? Thirty years I've been talking to that fish, and NOW he answers?
Boppy, that's what the Big One was like! Now you saw one too!
I saw one! And Deedee is going to believe me. That's worse. She'll want details.
A talking sock! All my life I've been losing socks, and THIS is where they go?
Excuse me, Mr. Sock. We haven't seen your other sock. We're very sorry.
Boppy, were YOU the one who cast it badly in 1997?
It was windy. Write that down. It was very windy.
The old reeds. I played back in there when I was nine. There's a sundial in a clearing. We called it Sundial Hollow.
He means please. Could you please shove over?
That's my boot! I lost that boot in 1988!
This is Sundial Hollow. I haven't been back here since I was nine.
It was green. All of this was green. Who took the green out of my hollow?
Tata! There's a fish in the SKY!
It's inside an orange block, like the dragonfly. It's just hanging there. Nothing is holding it up!
That fish jumped, and he never came down. Seventy-some years I've been fishing, and I never saw a fish stay up.
Tom. Get under it with the net.
It can't be moved. I tried one at the pond and one in California.
Then it won't hurt to hold the net.
I'm holding the net.
Good. Hold it better.
There's a little round hole in the side, like the dragonfly one had. I'm drawing it.
And there's Deedee's litter! On the clock rock!
Dragonfly: grey grass, orange block, round hole, burnt bulb. Fish: grey reeds, orange block, round hole, burnt bulb.
Lemon: grey tree, orange block, round hole, burnt bulb.
I'm writing that down too. In pen.
Somebody want to tell me what it means?
I don't know yet, Boppy. I'm only on page two.
Well, it's a small one anyway. Mine was double.
That's the Deep Pool. That's where Iron-Gill goes to sulk. Tom, you can put the net down.
And he has gold in his mustache!
First the Big One asks about me, and now this one. I'm very big with the fish, Tom.
You're a celebrity. I'll hold the net.
Gold like my teeth, with a fish on it! I got one! Cozy Rosie, I got one!
Boppy got treasure! Now your mouth matches your hat!
Put the date. Put the time. And put that he was THIS big.
Boppy, he was bigger than that.
First time in my life I ever undersold a fish.
Still up there. Somebody ought to let that fish finish his jump.
Old Iron-Gill. Forty years, Deary. I TOLD everybody.
I have proof. It's in my notebook. I drew his mustache.
Thank you, Cozy Rosie. Now. Let me look at him.
Look. I got gold. From the fish.
Fifty-one years I've been married to you, hubby, and you never once brought ME gold from a fish.
It's gold like my teeth!
I paid for those teeth.
Deedee, there's another orange block. There's a fish in it, and it's stuck up in the air over the water.
And more litter.
Three. My pond, California, and the marsh.
New rule. Nobody in this family goes anywhere alone. Not to the pond, not to the pier, not to the mailbox. Tom, that goes for Los Angeles too.
Yes, Mom.
Cut. Reset. Back to one. Everybody gets a touch-up.
All three sets are clear, and Stage 7 just unlocked itself. That's where the fog came from, so that's where my rack is.
Well, well, well...
Look who flew in for my big day. I'm on a forty-minute lunch. I spent thirty of it on the Metro.
Big shoot today. BACKLOT BEDLAM. Car chases, a saloon, a fake New York. I have forty costumes on one rack, and every single one is steamed.
Also, Olivia dropped Nara at your place again. Family trip to the desert. She's been howling at your front door since nine.
Then we get Nara. Then I watch you be very important. I'm not joking.
Very, very important. I have a lanyard.
Hi. Hi. Yes. I know. I was gone FOREVER. It was six days.
She's coming to set. I already asked. Nobody said yes, but nobody said no fast enough.
Ray, it's me. Wardrobe. I left eighty minutes ago. You waved.
Gone? It's a rack. It has wheels. It doesn't have ambitions.
Babe. Forty costumes. I steamed every single one. By hand. While humming.
Then we go get them back. Nara, stay close. This is a professional environment.
She's never eaten anything that fast. Not even my shoe.
The Backlot. Main Street up on the left, the Western street on the right, New York down on the left. All fake. All very expensive.
Nara. NARA. Don't...
That's a closed set! She's not on the call sheet!
She peed on the hydrant. That hydrant is fiberglass. That hydrant is a PROP.
She doesn't know that. Let her have this.
That's a costume tag. That's MY tag. WARDROBE, RACK 2, HAND WASH ONLY. I underlined it twice.
And it smells like grape fog juice. Only Stage 7 has a fog machine, so my rack must be in Stage 7.
Good girl. Professional environment, very good girl.
Those are the neatest cue cards I've ever seen. Is that calligraphy?
Main Street is clear. The bank is safe. The pie is still foam.
The Western street is clear. The horse can come out of its trailer now.
That was UNCALLED for!
New York is clear. It never looked better. It's plywood.
Somebody killed the work lights. And look, the catwalk is up. You only raise a catwalk when you're hiding something up there.
The stage set is at the top. The rack is up there. I can smell the steamer.
The main light rig runs the catwalk motor. If I get power back to it, the catwalk comes down.
Three junction boxes. They have to come up in the right order or the dimmer pops. The rig will tell us the order.
I fix everything with tape. You know this. Your kitchen drawer knows this.
My rack. MY RACK. All forty. Still steamed. Oh, I could cry.
Babe. It's a megaphone in a beret. It has notes.
This is a closed set. And you're not on the call sheet.
Back to one, everybody. Touch-ups.
Babe, when it says CUT, put WARDROBE on whoever is next. When it braces, Popcorn Jump. Or just tell it GREAT TAKE. Three times.
Forty. I counted. I'm going to count again. Forty.
I'm going to cry. I'm not going to cry. I'm a professional. I'm crying a little.
You're a professional. A crying professional. I'm so proud of you.
You know what this whole day was? A real steam-ulating experience.
Worth it?
You're the only uncle.
Which makes me the good one. By default. I'll take it.
Then we have ten minutes! I'll take all ten. I have so much to tell you.
A fish on Long Island jumped out of the water and froze in the air, inside one of those orange blocks. It's still hanging up there!
It's just hanging in the air? Babe! That's a flying fish!
And he's got more air time than you do.
Nobody has more air time than me. He's seven feet up. I was at thirty-six thousand.
And my mother made a rule. Nobody in the family goes anywhere alone, and that goes for Los Angeles too.
Nobody in the family. Does that count me?
You were the first one I thought of.
Then it's a good thing I got you this.
A lanyard! With my name on it! It's LAMINATED!
Of course it's laminated. I wanted this to last.
Do I have to give it back?
Never. Where I go, you go. That's Deedee's rule. So stick close, babe, and don't leave me hanging like that fish.
Very, very important. I have a lanyard. And now so do you.
She has to come. Nobody goes anywhere alone. Does she get a lanyard?
I only had one spare badge.
It says STUNT DOUBLE. Whose stunt double is she?
The horse's.
Nara! You're in the movies!
Hello, Ray. I'm Tom. I'm a visitor. It says so right here.
He didn't even look at it.
He never looks. But you held it up beautifully.
A flash! What kind of flash?
I've seen grumpy things like that! On my street, and at my parents' pond. They always show up right after a flash.
I'm hired! I've been a visitor for one hour!
She's the stunt double! She has a badge!
You can tell it's grape from one sniff?
